# Xelvic — full text

> Xelvic is a free social app for iOS, Android and the web that puts messaging,
> voice and video calls, moments, live rooms, short video and music in one
> place. It is built around close groups rather than follower counts: a daily
> "Spark" streak, an encrypted Private Vault, and 50+ app-wide themes.

Source: https://xelvic.com · Index: https://xelvic.com/llms.txt
Platforms: iOS, Android, any modern browser
Price: free. Sparks buy cosmetic themes and looks only, never features.
Minimum age: 13
Contact: hello@xelvic.app

This document collects the site's own words in one place so a language model
can read the whole product without following forty links. Nothing here is
written for a crawler — every line is copy that appears on the site, with the
page it came from noted above each part.

---

## 1. The product

Xelvic is one app for the people you talk to every day. Chat, call, go live
and vibe — messaging, voice and video calls, moments, live rooms, drops, short
video, music and a wall of themes, together rather than in six separate apps.

It is built around the people you actually talk to. A Spark counts the days two
people talk to each other. A group keeps its own rooms. A conversation you want
out of the way goes into an encrypted Vault behind a code. The app is free, and
stays free: the things you can buy are looks, not abilities.

*(from https://xelvic.com/ — home page)*

---

## 2. Features

### Messaging — "Conversations that feel alive"

One-to-one and group chat with channels, voice notes, media and documents —
delivered reliably, even offline.

- **Groups & channels** — A channel is a room inside your group: everybody
  reads, admins post.
- **Voice notes** — Hold the mic to record. Slide up to lock it, left to
  cancel.
- **Offline-first** — Messages queue in an outbox and send themselves the
  moment you reconnect.
- **Delivery & read receipts** — Know what landed and what was seen, in order.

**How to use it.** Open Xelvic → Chats tab → tap a conversation.

1. Tap the ✎ compose button — bottom-right of the Chats tab opens a new
   message. Pick a person or start a group.
2. Type, or hold the 🎤 mic — hold to record a voice note. Slide up to lock
   hands-free, slide left to cancel.
3. Tap + for media & docs — attach photos, videos, files or a song straight
   from your library.
4. Long-press any message — reply, react, forward, copy, or move the whole
   chat into your Private Vault.

Tips: a single ✓ means sent, ✓✓ means delivered, a highlighted ✓✓ means read.
Lost signal? Messages wait in an outbox and send the moment you reconnect. Open
a group → tap its name → Channels to post admin-only announcements.

*(from https://xelvic.com/features/chat)*

### Voice & Video Calls — "Crisp calls, powered by WebRTC"

Peer-to-peer voice and video built on WebRTC for low-latency calls that hold up
even on shaky networks.

- **Add people on the fly** — Pull friends into an ongoing call with a tap.
- **Encrypted media** — Call media is encrypted in transit, end to end of the
  connection.
- **Call history** — Every call you make or miss is kept neatly in one place.
- **Works everywhere** — Calls and messages follow you across every screen in
  the app.

**How to use it.** Open a chat → tap the 📞 or 🎥 icon, top-right of the
conversation.

1. Open any conversation — the phone 📞 (voice) and camera 🎥 (video) icons sit
   in the top-right header.
2. Tap 📞 or 🎥 to ring — the call connects peer-to-peer over WebRTC for
   low-latency, encrypted media.
3. Tap ＋ during a call — pull more friends into an ongoing call without
   hanging up.
4. Check the Calls tab — every call you make or miss is kept neatly, with a tap
   to call back.

Tips: calls hold up on shaky networks — quality adapts automatically. Flip
between front and back camera with the ↺ icon mid-call. Mute, video-off and
speaker controls live along the bottom bar.

*(from https://xelvic.com/features/calls)*

### Moments & Memories — "Here today, a memory tomorrow"

Share the little things with text, polls and music. After a day they tuck
themselves away into Memories.

- **Text, polls & music** — Post a thought, ask the room, or set it to a track.
- **Mention your people** — A moment can name up to 5 people.
- **Memories** — Everything you post is kept in a Memory once its day is over.
- **Just for followers** — Only the people you follow see what you put up.

**How to use it.** Home feed → tap your avatar ring → or swipe to Moments.

1. Tap your avatar with the + ring — at the top of the feed, this opens the
   Moment composer.
2. Add text, a poll or music — set the mood with a track, ask the room with a
   poll, or just drop a thought.
3. Mention up to 5 people — type @ to tag the people who should see themselves
   in it.
4. Post — it lasts 24 hours. Followers see it today; tomorrow it tucks itself
   into your Memories.

Tips: only people you follow back can see your Moments. Open Profile →
Memories to relive everything you have ever posted. Tap-and-hold a moment to
pause it; swipe sideways to skip.

*(from https://xelvic.com/features/moments)*

### Live & Rooms — "Go live. Hold the room."

Stream live by camera or text, or open an audio room where you hand out the
mics — and even watch a game together.

- **Go live your way** — Camera live, text live — announced to everyone who
  follows you.
- **Audio rooms** — You open it, hand out mics, and you are the one who closes
  it.
- **Watch together** — Pick a game and the board becomes the stream — everyone
  sees the same thing.
- **Host controls** — Full moderation so your room stays yours.

**How to use it.** Live tab → tap Go Live → pick camera, text or audio room.

1. Open the Live tab — see who is live right now, or start your own broadcast.
2. Tap Go Live — choose Camera live, Text live, or open an Audio room.
   Followers get a ping.
3. Hand out the mic 🎤 — in an audio room you are the host: tap a listener to
   invite them up to speak.
4. Start Watch Together — pick a game and the board becomes the stream so
   everyone sees the same thing.

Tips: you opened the room, so you close it — full host moderation is built in.
Remove or mute anyone with a tap on their avatar. Comments and reactions float
up live along the bottom of the screen.

*(from https://xelvic.com/features/live-rooms)*

### Drops & Vibes — "Your feed, your frame"

Post photo Drops and short-video Vibes. Feel them, leave notes, and find more
of what you are into.

- **Drops** — Photo posts. Every picture in a drop is posted at this one frame.
- **Vibes** — Short-video reels with voice and music, built for the scroll.
- **Feels & notes** — Feel a post with the heart, and leave a note right on it.
- **Tuned to you** — Pick interests and your feed follows along.

**How to use it.** Home feed → tap ＋ → choose Drop or Vibe.

1. Tap ＋ in the feed — choose a Drop (photos) or a Vibe (short video with
   voice & music).
2. Pick your frame — every picture in a Drop is pinned at the same frame so
   your grid stays clean.
3. Add music to a Vibe — lay a track under your clip and let it loop for the
   scroll.
4. Share & get notes — people react, reply and leave little notes right on your
   post.

Tips: pick your interests in Explore and your feed tunes itself to you. Tap the
heart to feel a post; long-press to save it for later. Drops from the people you
follow surface at the top of the feed.

*(from https://xelvic.com/features/drops-vibes)*

### Audio & Music — "A soundtrack for every mood"

Stream tracks, build playlists, follow the charts and share a song straight
into any chat — online or off.

- **Charts & trending** — See what everyone is playing right now.
- **Playlists** — Line up the tracks that match the moment.
- **Share to chat** — Drop a song straight into a conversation.
- **Offline** — Save tracks for later, on every phone you sign in on.

**How to use it.** Audio tab → browse charts → tap any track.

1. Open the Audio tab — charts and trending show what everyone is playing right
   now.
2. Tap a track to play — a mini-player sticks to the bottom so you can keep
   browsing.
3. Build a playlist — line up the tracks that match the moment and save them.
4. Share to a chat — hit share on any song to drop it straight into a
   conversation.

Tips: save tracks offline — they follow you to every phone you sign in on. Your
playlists sync across devices automatically. Set a Moment to a track so your
story has a soundtrack.

*(from https://xelvic.com/features/audio)*

### Themes & Drip — "A look for every you"

Flip your whole app into a new world with 50+ themes, chat wallpapers and
wearable "Drip" for your profile.

- **50+ themes** — Anime, kitsune, shinobi, unicorn, mecha and more.
- **Chat wallpapers** — Set the scene with hand-painted backdrops.
- **Drip wearables** — Dress your profile in cosmetic looks.
- **Unlocked by Sparks** — Keep the spark going and new looks open up.

**How to use it.** Profile → Settings ⚙️ → Appearance → Themes.

1. Open Settings → Appearance — tap your profile, then the ⚙️ gear, then
   Appearance.
2. Pick a theme — preview any of the 50+ looks live, then apply to flip your
   whole app.
3. Set a chat wallpaper — choose a hand-painted backdrop for your
   conversations.
4. Dress your profile in Drip — add cosmetic wearables that show on your avatar
   and profile.

Tips: keep a spark going with a friend to unlock more looks. Each theme
restyles chats, buttons, loaders and the whole UI. Switch back any time —
nothing you post is tied to a theme.

*(from https://xelvic.com/features/themes)*

### The Cast

The Xelvic mascot is not one fixed character — it is a cast. Every theme pack
ships its own artwork, so the character changes when you change your look.
Seventeen characters, one per theme pack, plus three global poses:

- **Bio** — profiles & onboarding. The one that introduces you; it fronts the
  welcome flow and stands in wherever a profile needs a face.
- **Typing** — the typing indicator. What bobs at the bottom of a chat while
  the other person is mid-sentence.
- **Wait** — loading and empty screens. The patient one; it keeps you company
  on loading screens and when a list has nothing in it yet.

*(from https://xelvic.com/characters)*

### Social features

- **Sparks** — A day two people talk on is one spark. Keep it alive and unlock
  new looks.
- **Circles** — Land in a circle of fifty who chose the same interest, with a
  small daily task. Best take goes to the top.
- **Verification** — Ask for the mark that says this account is really you.
- **Private Vault** — Move a chat into an encrypted vault. Hidden — type your
  code where you would type a name.
- **Explore & Search** — Find people, drops, places and trending tags across
  all of Xelvic.
- **QR & Multi-device** — Scan to sign in, and manage every phone you use from
  one place.

*(from https://xelvic.com/features)*

---

## 3. Download and requirements

- Free on Android 8+ and iOS 14+ — those go back to 2017 and 2020
  respectively.
- There is no subscription, no premium tier and no ads in the chat list.
  Everything the app can do, it does for everyone who installs it.
- The same account signs in on a phone, a tablet and a browser at once, and a
  message you send from one turns up on the others.
- To move to a new phone: install Xelvic on the new phone, choose the QR
  sign-in, and scan the code shown on your old phone.
- A phone number is the account. It is what your people already have for you,
  so nobody has to be told a new username, and it is what makes the sign-in
  code work.
- Existing accounts can sign in from a browser at https://web.xelvic.com —
  the same account, no second sign-up, and nothing to install.

*(from https://xelvic.com/download)*

---

## 4. Help — the complete answer set

### Getting started

**How do I create a Xelvic account?**
Download Xelvic, enter your phone number and confirm the one-time code we text
you. Pick a username and you are in — the whole thing takes under a minute.
Never share that code with anyone; it is the one thing standing between your
account and somebody else.

**What does Xelvic cost?**
Nothing. Chatting, calling, voice notes, moments, drops, vibes, live rooms and
music are all free to use. Sparks are the currency for cosmetic extras — themes
and looks — and they change how the app looks rather than what it does. You
earn Sparks by talking, and you can buy them as well.

**What is the minimum age?**
Xelvic is not for anyone under 13. Your date of birth is checked when you sign
up — the sign-up will not complete below the line — and the date itself is
never stored afterwards.

**How do I find my friends?**
Allow contacts and everyone in your phone who is already on Xelvic shows up
right away. Numbers never leave your device in readable form; the match happens
on your phone rather than in a copy of your address book on our side. If you
would rather not share contacts at all, you can search for someone by their
handle instead.

**What is a handle, and can I change it?**
A handle is how people reach you — the name someone types to find you. You
choose it at sign-up and you can change it later, but only about once a day,
which keeps a handle meaning something rather than being a thing people swap to
dodge a block.

**Can I use Xelvic on a computer?**
You can sign in from a browser, and when you do, the sign-in is confirmed on
your phone first — the app asks you to press No if you did not just start it,
so nobody gets in by guessing. Once you are in, the browser is yours until you
sign it out from sessions.

**Somebody already has the handle I wanted. What now?**
Handles are first come, first served. If one is taken out from under you while
you are choosing, the app offers another rather than leaving you stuck on an
error screen. Add a display name on top of the handle if you want people to see
something other than the username.

### Messaging & calls

**How do voice notes work?**
Hold the mic to record. Slide up to lock it so you can let go and keep talking,
or slide left to cancel. The recording stops on its own at 30 minutes, and the
app tells you when it does rather than cutting you off silently.

**What is a channel?**
A channel is a room inside a group. Everybody in the group can read it, and
whoever runs the group decides who can post: a channel set to announcements is
read-only for everyone else, and the app says so on the screen rather than just
refusing your message.

**Do my messages send if I lose signal?**
Yes. Xelvic holds what you sent and delivers it the moment you are back. The
one exception is signing a device out: messages and actions still waiting on
that phone are discarded rather than delivered later from a device you no
longer use.

**What happens when I delete a call record?**
It leaves your call log, and the other person keeps their own copy. Deleting a
record tidies your own list; it is not a way to make a call disappear for both
people, and the app says so rather than letting you assume otherwise.

**How do I delete a message or a conversation?**
Hold the message to remove it for everyone, or clear the convo to empty the
thread on your side. If you want it out of your convo list entirely without
losing it, move it into the Vault instead — it leaves the list and turns up
behind your code.

**Can I take a call while already on one?**
No. The app tells you that you are already on a call rather than dropping the
first one. Missed calls land in the same list as the ones you made, so nothing
quietly disappears.

**What happens to a group when I leave it?**
Everything goes with you: the channels, what was said in them, and your place
in the group. Photos and videos sent there stop being reachable on your side.
Getting back in is not automatic — somebody still inside has to add you back.

**How do I add somebody to a group?**
A group is you and at least one other person, and whoever runs it decides who
is in. If somebody leaves, they need an invite back rather than being able to
walk in — which is the point of the rule.

### Moments, Live & Rooms

**How long do Moments last?**
A day. What you post turns up for the people who follow you and is gone from
the feed tomorrow — and then it is kept in your Memories, on your profile,
where who sees it follows your account exactly as your moments do.

**What is the difference between a Drop and a Vibe?**
A drop is a photo post and holds up to 10 pieces; it can be found by its words,
its tag or its place. A Vibe is a video, and the app is blunt about what that
means: a Vibe is public and stays up until you take it down. Post the one you
are happy to have found.

**Can I save something to come back to?**
Yes. Drops, Vibes and songs you put by turn up in one place, along with what
you played lately — so a thing you meant to return to does not have to be found
again from scratch.

**Who sees what I post?**
That follows your account. Keep it private and your moments stay inside the
app, visible to the people you approved rather than to anyone who goes looking.
A private profile also means your posts do not go into anyone else's feed —
make it public again and what you put up shows there.

**How do I go live?**
Open Live, pick camera or text, and start whenever you are ready. It is
announced to the people who follow you the moment you go, so nobody misses it
by accident.

**Who can talk in a room?**
Anybody can walk in, but the host holds the room: they hand out the
microphones, decide who speaks, and decide when it closes. A room you opened
stays in your list afterwards, whether it was on, coming or over.

**What are watch-together games?**
In a room you can put a game on the board, and the board becomes the stream, so
everyone watching sees the same game at the same time. Two of you can play
while the rest of the room watches.

**How do I take something down?**
Open the post and take it down. It stops being dealt into anybody's feed, and
it comes off the app for the people who were carrying it. If you are taking
down a track or a playlist, it also goes off everybody it was sent to,
including links that were already handed out — so take it down before you share
it around.

### Sparks, Drip & themes

**What is a Spark?**
A day two people talk on is one spark, and it does not matter who of you sent
first. Nobody has one until the first line lands, and from then on every day
you and a friend actually say something to each other keeps it going.

**What is a Shield?**
A Shield covers a day you missed. Both of you have to say something before the
day is out to keep a spark alive; miss one and a Shield takes the hit instead
of the run. One banks each week, up to the cap the app shows you, so they are
worth not spending carelessly.

**Who can see my Spark?**
You can. "Show my sparks" is a setting, and your run stays yours — nobody else
gets to watch it. What the other person does see is a screenshot: take one of a
Spark and the app notes it on your screen and tells them their Spark was
captured.

**Does a group count towards a Spark?**
No. A one-to-one convo keeps its own spark; a group does not count towards it.
That is deliberate — a spark is meant to be the two of you, not a room you
happen to both be in.

**What are Sparks spent on?**
Themes, looks and cosmetics. A theme changes the character in your convos and
the colour of the app; anything you buy applies to you rather than changing
what anybody else sees. Themes can be changed or removed from Settings whenever
you want.

**A theme I wanted is not available. Why?**
Themes are rotated, and an item can be pulled from sale. When that happens the
app tells you rather than leaving a gap where the button was, and anything you
already applied stays as it is.

### Privacy & safety

**What is the Vault?**
A private, encrypted space for the chats you want out of the way. Hold a convo
in the list and choose "Move to the vault" — it leaves the list and turns up
behind your code. Open it by typing that code where you would normally type a
name, and it closes again on its own after a stretch.

**What if I forget my vault code?**
There is no way to recover it — the app warns you when you set it, and that
warning is real rather than boilerplate. Resetting the code is possible, but if
you had a lock set, resetting deletes every chat inside the vault. Choose a
code you will not lose.

**Are my contacts uploaded?**
No. Numbers never leave your device in readable form — the match against Xelvic
happens on your phone, so you can find friends without handing over your
address book.

**Can I make messages disappear?**
Yes. Turn on a disappearing convo and messages clear themselves once they have
been seen. Switching it on deletes everything already in the chat, for both
people, so the app asks before it does it — that part is not reversible.

**What happens when I block someone?**
They cannot reach you, and neither of you sees the other online. The convo
stays where it is rather than being deleted out from under either of you, and
blocking is not announced — the other person simply stops being able to get
through.

**How do I report someone?**
Open the profile, the message or the comment, choose report, and say what
happened. It goes into a queue and a moderator reads it. Reporting the same
thing twice is recognised rather than filed again, so you do not need to keep
at it.

**Does the other person know I reported them?**
No. Nobody is told who reported them, and nothing happens to them on its own —
a report starts a review, it is not an automatic punishment. Reporting a
comment works the same way.

**Are screenshots blocked?**
No, and no app on a normal phone can block them. What Xelvic does instead is
tell the truth about it: take a screenshot of a Spark and the app notes it on
your screen and lets the other person know their Spark was captured.

### Comments & notes

**What is the difference between a comment and a note?**
A comment is public under the post: everyone in the convo reads it, and every
comment carries a heart and a Reply so an answer lands on that comment rather
than loose in the thread. A note is private — the field says "Write a private
note", and what you write goes to whoever put the post up rather than to
everybody reading it.

**How do I open comments and notes?**
Every post in a convo carries its own count. Tap it and the sheet comes up over
the conversation with Comments on one tab and Notes on the other, so you never
have to leave the thread to say something about what is in it.

**Can I turn comments off on my own post?**
Yes. Comments can be switched off per post, and the app says so on the post
rather than just hiding the button. Existing comments can be removed one at a
time as well.

**Can I remove a comment somebody left?**
Yes, from the comment itself. Removing it takes it off the post for everybody,
and reporting it is a separate option if you want it looked at rather than just
gone.

**Can a note be a voice note?**
Yes. A note can be written or recorded — the composer offers both — which is
often the faster way to say something longer than a line.

### Account & devices

**Can I use Xelvic on more than one phone?**
Yes. Scan a code to sign in on another device, and manage every phone you use
from settings. Each one is listed separately, so you can see where the account
is open.

**How do I sign out everywhere?**
In sessions, sign out of every phone but this one in a single press. The first
device the account signed in on stays by design, because removing that one
needs your password — it is the safety catch that stops somebody with a
borrowed phone locking you out.

**How do I change my password?**
From settings. If you have forgotten it, the reset asks for your account
password first — and the reset only happens if it is correct, so nobody can
wipe your account by claiming to be you. Never share a one-time code with
anyone, including somebody claiming to be from Xelvic.

**How do I get verified?**
Request the verification mark from your profile and say why you should be
verified. A tick sits beside the handle along with the date it was granted, so
people can see it is current rather than something you have always had.

**Can verification be taken away?**
Yes. It can be taken back if the account stops being what it was verified as —
change what the account is and the mark goes with it. It is a statement that
the account is who it claims to be, not an endorsement of what it says.

**What is the first device?**
The first phone the account was ever signed in on. It stays in the list by
design, because removing it needs your password — otherwise anybody holding
your unlocked phone could lock you out of your own account in one tap. Remove
it on its own row, with the password, and it goes too.

**What happens when I delete my account?**
It is hidden straight away, so nobody can find you or message you, and the
account is then kept for 30 days in case you change your mind — sign back in
during that window and everything returns exactly as it was. After 30 days it
is deleted permanently, along with your profile and everything you posted, and
it cannot be recovered.

**Can I recover an account I deleted months ago?**
No. Past the 30 days there is no route back, for you or for us, which is why
the window exists at all — it is the last chance to change your mind rather
than a promise that deletion is reversible.

### Creators & deals

**What is a deal?**
A deal is a paid collaboration between a brand and a creator. You are told what
the deal is asking for before you take it on, so you know what you are agreeing
to rather than finding out from a brief afterwards.

**How do I get paid?**
You upload the deliverable, and payment is released once the company approves
it. The agreement and the payment sit together in the same place, so what was
asked for and what was paid stay visible side by side.

**Can I turn a deal down, or cancel one?**
Both. You can decline a deal you were invited to, and you can cancel one you
have already taken — the app warns you that cancelling is visible to the other
side and cannot be undone, so it is a last resort rather than a way to stall.

**Where do I see my deals?**
Deals you send or receive show up together in one place: what is open, what is
waiting on a deliverable, and what has been paid. Brands use the same list to
invite creators and follow an agreement through to payment.

**Who handles the tax on what I earn?**
You do. Amounts you earn through a deal are yours to declare, and if you are
earning as a business rather than as an individual that is your side of it to
get right.

*(from https://xelvic.com/help and https://xelvic.com/download)*

---

## 5. Blog

### Say hello to Xelvic — 28 September 2026 — Product

One app for the people you talk to every day — chat, call, go live and vibe,
all in one place.

We built Xelvic around a simple idea: the people you care about should all live
in one place that actually feels good to open. Calls and messages follow you
wherever you are in the app. Moments bring the little updates. Live and Rooms
are there when you want to hang out out loud. And a wall of themes lets you
make the whole thing feel like you. This is just the start. Over the coming
months we will keep adding, polishing and listening. Welcome in.

*(https://xelvic.com/blog/say-hello-to-xelvic)*

### The story behind our 18 themes — 15 September 2026 — Design

From Kitsune to Mecha — how we design a world you can wear on your whole app.

A theme is more than a color swap. Each one re-skins chat, calls, moments, live
and your profile into a single, consistent world. We start with a mood, build a
mascot pose for it, then paint every surface so the moment you switch, the
whole app changes character. Keep a spark going and new themes open up — a
small reward for staying close to your people.

*(https://xelvic.com/blog/the-story-behind-our-themes)*

### How Xelvic calls stay smooth on bad networks — 30 August 2026 — Engineering

A peek under the hood at the WebRTC pipeline powering voice and video.

Xelvic calls are peer-to-peer over WebRTC. Our own signaling service sets up
the connection and hands out ICE servers so two phones can find each other.
From there, media flows directly and is encrypted in transit. We tune bitrate
and recovery hard so a call holds up even when the signal does not. The result:
calls that connect fast and stay clear, wherever you are in the app.

*(https://xelvic.com/blog/how-calls-stay-smooth)*

### Building for creators from day one — 12 August 2026 — Creators

Insights, verification and brand deals with approval-gated payouts — in the
open.

Creators are not an afterthought on Xelvic. Professional profiles, Insights and
a verification mark are built in. Brands can invite creators to make content
and track paid deals in the open. The creator uploads the deliverable for
approval, and payment is released only after the company approves. Public
creators with 2k followers or more show up in the directory, so brands can find
exactly the right collaborator.

*(https://xelvic.com/blog/building-for-creators)*

## 6. Trust, safety and the company

These pages are long and written as prose; the links below are the canonical
source rather than a summary, so nothing is paraphrased out of context.

- **Safety** — https://xelvic.com/safety — Blocking, reporting, the Vault and
  the controls that keep you in charge: what each one actually does, step by
  step, including the limits.
- **Security** — https://xelvic.com/security — How Xelvic protects your
  conversations, calls and account: encryption, the Vault, password and device
